what: Overnight 2026-10-12 (user-authorised, exploratory, not the pre-registered round-2 window): tune Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as the GPU reviewer/lead on the V620s and re-test it. Five replays of the same 27 harvested W3 review rounds (replay-7..10, plus replay-1 = qwen3.8 for reference), two GPU serving sweeps, and one harness bug found and fixed (ripgrep).

setup.server: transient llama-server inside LXC 151 (production chat stopped for the night; window open = perturbers stopped), unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF UD-Q4_K_M, 1 slot, thinking off via chat-template kwargs, keyed with the trial's throwaway key, reached from the sandbox through a locked policy extended with 192.168.6.151:8090
setup.harness: feat/wf-experiment: replay-reviews --reviewer-model w1/qwen3.6 --worker http://192.168.6.151:8090/v1 plus the per-run options below

gpu_sweeps.workload: the largest real review packet (11,467 tokens) cold (prefill), warm (generation), and doubled (~23K tokens) cold

round_1.error: ROCm illegal memory access at load (not pursued)

gpu_sweeps.chosen: layer split 1:1, ubatch 1024, batch 2048, f16 KV, flash attention, ctx 131072: +19% prefill and +11% generation over replay-7's settings; measured in a real replay: prompt 1632 -> 1883 t/s, generation 53.7 -> 65.5 t/s

ripgrep_bug.finding: the sandbox VM had no `rg` on PATH; opencode then tries to download ripgrep into each fresh per-task home, which the locked policy blocks, so EVERY glob and grep call by every agent (reviewers and CPU implementers) failed after a long timeout ('ripgrep execution failed').
ripgrep_bug.evidence: tool time per 27-round replay - replay-1 (qwen3.8): grep 40.5 + glob 9.0 min of a 75-min session wall; replay-7: glob 36.6 + grep 5.4 of 41; replay-8: glob 45.3 + grep 18.0 of 60. After installing ripgrep: replay-9 tool time 0.5 min of 18.6; replay-10 0.8 of 16.9.
ripgrep_bug.impact: every measured run so far (W1, W3, all replays before replay-9) paid this: reviews ran 2-4x slower than the model required, and implementers' searches failed too. The W3 throughput numbers include it.
ripgrep_bug.fix: ripgrep 14.1.1 installed in VM 176 tonight (host-downloaded trixie package, checksum-verified, through the guest agent); wf-sandbox-provision.sh now installs ripgrep and dies if rg is missing (ef6a8f0).

temperature_bug.finding: opencode sends an agent's temperature only for a model marked temperature-capable; our provider definitions were not, so --reviewer-temperature 0.2 had no effect (replay-8 ran at the server's 0.7). Fixed in f8a9f9d: the reviewer's provider model is marked capable and the other agents on that provider are pinned to 0.7 explicitly (marking it would otherwise make opencode send its own default to them). Verified on the server's /slots: 23 of 27 in-flight requests at 0.2; the other 4 are opencode's session-title requests at 0.5.

replays.note: rg broken; 7 one-step verdicts; trial-1 hallucinations returned; caught both qwen3.8 misses

replays.options: read-first, enforce-read, 30 steps, temp 0.7 (temperature not yet sent)
replays.note: rg broken; enforce-read flipped 4 one-step REVISEs to ACCEPT - fixed one hallucination but also dropped a real catch (w2-05 r1); net zero, not kept
rg FIXED; too strict - ~6 REVISEs were nits or self-contradicting; but 2 real catches nobody else made

BEST: 3 real defects qwen3.8 accepted (w2-05 r0 and r1 both FAIL the hidden tests; the should_cache TypeError), misses 1 real bug qwen3.8 caught (redirect urljoin) and 1 incomplete-request REVISE (w2-07 r0); 2-3 borderline REVISEs remain

hidden_test_grading.w2-05 r0: 1 failed, 12 passed - REVISEd by Qwen3.6 in replays 9 and 10; accepted by qwen3.8 and by W3's reviewer
hidden_test_grading.w2-05 r1: 1 failed, 12 passed - REVISEd by Qwen3.6 in trial 1, replay-7 and replay-10; accepted by qwen3.8 and W3
hidden_test_grading.others_contested: w2-01 r1/r2, w2-02, w2-11, w2-12, w2-13, w2-16 states all pass their hidden tests

conclusion.reviewer: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on the V620s with read-first + defects-only + temperature 0.2 is at least qwen3.8's equal as a reviewer on these 27 rounds (15/20 vs 16/20 W3 agreement, but it catches the two hidden-test-failing states qwen3.8 accepts) and 4.5x faster per review (44 s vs 201 s). The previous 'roughly 2x' projection was conservative because of the ripgrep bug.
conclusion.settings: keep: tuned server (layer 1:1, ub 1024, f16 KV), read-first, defects-only, reviewer temperature 0.2, REVIEW_STEPS 30. Drop: enforce-read (net zero).
conclusion.caveat: single replays at sampling temperature > 0 are noisy (same model, same rule moved 14 -> 17 -> 14 -> 12 -> 15 agreement across runs); differences of 1-2 rounds are within noise. The ripgrep fix also changes the baseline for qwen3.8: a re-run of replay-1 with ripgrep would make the speed comparison fair.
